value.hook: Open when a test or daemon hangs at 0% CPU, when a reader joined after shutdown never returns, or before committing a merge that had conflicts
value.title: Rare hangs: reproduce by looping the exact child, sample it, then probe the kernel primitive alone (F273); merge-commit trailers after a conflict

sections.name: body
sections.value:
- **A 1-in-1000 hang needs a loop that is parallel and kills only its own processes.** Run the re-executed test child directly: `<test-bin> --exact <name> --nocapture` with the child env var set, 16 at a time at nice 19, `start_new_session=True`. On timeout, `sample <pid> 2 -file …` and `lsof -p`, then `killpg` that run's own group. For F273 the counts were 4 hangs in 20,000 before the fix and 0 after; keep both logs as receipts (`/tmp/f273-repro/child-*.log`). Looping the whole suite 30 times showed nothing; looping the child did.
- **Then isolate the primitive in a throwaway crate in /tmp** (`[workspace]` in its Cargo.toml, `nice -n 19 cargo build --release`), run 8 copies in parallel, and count. macOS AF_UNIX finding: a reader already blocked in `recv` on a `UnixStream::pair` can miss the peer's `shutdown(Write)` wakeup (a few per million). After that a second shutdown, or `shutdown(Read)` on its own end, returns ENOTCONN and wakes nothing. Only a read timeout recovers it, at the next read, with the partial line intact. The rule: **any thread that joins a socket reader after shutdown needs that reader to use a bounded read** (daemon_log `READ_RECHECK` = 1 s).
- **Refute your first theory with a probe before you write it down.** "std's non-atomic CLOEXEC pipe leaks into a sibling" looked right; 5,000 aggressive spawns showed 0 leaks, so it went nowhere near the PR.
- **Tests that wait on a child: use `try_wait` with a scaled deadline, write stderr to a file, and kill your own pid on timeout.** `Command::output()` waits on a pipe's EOF with no bound.
- **shared-build now stops a `cargo test` past `PIJ_SHARED_BUILD_TEST_LIMIT`** (20 min, scaled; exit 8; it names what was still in cargo's group). For a known-long run, set the limit higher or to 0.
- **After a merge with conflicts, commit with an explicit `-m` that carries the trailers.** `git commit --no-edit` keeps the `# Conflicts:` lines as the last paragraph, so `Pij-Seat`/`Pij-Prime` stop being trailers. If it is already pushed, amend and `--force-with-lease=<branch>:<sha>` before anyone reviews.
- **Every tool call has a cost.** Chaining `cmd | grep -v …; next` hid a failed push in one call: grep exited 1 and its output vanished. Always `git ls-remote` after each push, in its own call.
